title: TeardownResponse
description: Response body of POST /api/workspace/teardown (HEL-366). Always HTTP 200, both for a clean and a blocked call — a block is an expected, informative outcome, not a client error. `committed` is true only when every resource tagged `tag` was actually deleted (a real, non-dry-run call with no conflicts); it is false for a dry run AND for a blocked call. `blocked` is true whenever `conflicts` is non-empty, in which case NOTHING was deleted (all-or-nothing) and the delete counts are all zero. The `*Deleted` counts report what was actually deleted on a real committed call, or what WOULD be deleted on a clean dry run — never a partial figure. HEL-904: `typesDeleted` is removed -- Outputs are torn down transitively via ON DELETE CASCADE from their owning pipeline, not independently counted.

dashboardsDeleted.description: HEL-907 evaluator-1 CR3: dashboards joined data_sources/pipelines as a taggable, torn-down-together resource kind. A tagged dashboard's panels cascade via the pre-existing panels.dashboard_id ON DELETE CASCADE — no separate guard/count for panels.

TeardownConflict.description: One blocking conflict: a tagged resource that would be (or was, for a dry run) blocked, and why — refuse-on-out-of-batch-dependent (design.md Decision 2/6) or an existing per-DataType delete guard (panel-bound / still-linked source companion).

resourceKind.description: Only this kind carries a blocking guard — a tagged Pipeline has no analogous dependent-of-a-Pipeline guard, and Outputs (HEL-904) cascade with their owning pipeline instead of carrying a guard of their own.
